rule: GOAL: Match the top row's items to the middle slots. CONTROLS: Click an item to select it; click a destination to swap. RULE: The shortest solution uses the fewest swaps, not the fewest clicks. TRAP: Assuming all items must move to the bottom first wastes time.

GOAL: Guide the piece from the start to the exit using the shortest path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece two tiles at a time across white squares. RULE: Only white tiles are walkable; gray tiles act as walls. TRAP: Assuming you could move one tile at a time, causing wasted actions.

GOAL: Move the purple marker along the diagonal line into the gray blob. CONTROLS: Click a dot to jump the marker to it. RULE: Jumps are limited to three positions along the line. TRAP: Assuming the pulse animation indicated a valid move; it only showed the click location.

GOAL: Move the handle right to clear the white barrier. CONTROLS: Click the blue button to shift the handle right, rotating the wall around the yellow gap. RULE: The top and bottom wall positions sum to a constant; moving one side rotates the other in opposite directions. TRAP: Assuming the black line’s left edge tracks the top white boundary; it extends further left initially, confusing position tracking.

GOAL: Align the green player's left edge with the boundary at column 8. CONTROLS: Four buttons shift the staircase boundaries; clicks adjust the wall's position relative to the player. RULE: Moving the player left decreases the bottom boundary's column index, tightening the white space. TRAP: Assuming barriers are movable obstacles; they are static decorations that do not affect the solution path.

GOAL: Move a blue box to a marked spot using a carrying mechanic. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player and carry the box; Space grabs or drops it. RULE: Movement translates the stack; direction changes do not flip the box’s position relative to the player. TRAP: Believing moving down while carrying flips the box to the bottom; it actually stays on top.

GOAL: Align five vertical boundaries to specific heights using barrier constraints. CONTROLS: Click columns between strips to shift boundary positions by two units. RULE: Boundaries cannot cross barrier tops; order of operations matters to avoid illegal intermediate states. TRAP: Assuming boundary limits depend only on final barrier positions, ignoring that intermediate states must also satisfy all constraints.

GOAL: Arrange symbols to match a hidden sequence. CONTROLS: Click slots to swap symbols. Space submits the arrangement. RULE: Feedback reveals the longest correct prefix of your order. TRAP: Assuming adjacent slots imply adjacent sequence positions; the pipe may reverse flow direction.

GOAL: Reach the key without letting the guard land on you. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player one tile per turn. RULE: The guard jumped two tiles toward you if you ended your move in his row within three tiles. TRAP: Assuming distance four was safe; it wasn't, as the guard reacted to the new position after your move.

GOAL: Fill seven slots to match the target sequence using colored rings from the tray. CONTROLS: Click two items to swap their positions; press Space to submit the solution. RULE: Head markers in the main row expand into the corresponding colored boxes' slots, preserving order. TRAP: Assuming the target length equals the main row's slot count ignores the expansion, causing a mismatch.

GOAL: Fill seven target slots by inserting a three-piece green group into a five-slot red row. CONTROLS: Click items to swap positions between the tray and slots. Press space to confirm the final arrangement. RULE: The head piece replaces one red slot with the entire green group, expanding the total length. TRAP: Assuming the head adds a new position rather than substituting the existing red slot.

GOAL: Fill the white cross cells with green using the sliding tip. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicking white cells turns them green; LEFT absorbs the shape. RULE: The tip must align with a cell to change it; the top cell initially resisted clicks. TRAP: The first action after reset is swallowed by the animation, wasting a move if you click immediately.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks to form the target sequence by placing two identical blue triples. CONTROLS: Click blocks to swap positions; press space to submit the arrangement. RULE: The blue box repeats exactly, so its contents must match the repeated pattern in the target. TRAP: Assuming each block moves independently; the shared blue triple links multiple positions simultaneously.

GOAL: Arrange colored tiles into three boxes to form a specific nine-tile sequence. CONTROLS: Click a tray item, then a box slot to move it. Spacebar submits the solution. RULE: The final sequence groups tiles by box, starting with each box's pre-filled tile. TRAP: Assuming red slots hold colors; they actually hold head markers that order the groups.

GOAL: Shrink the key tip by matching its cross-section to the reference pad, then slide it up through the narrowed shaft to the head. CONTROLS: Click pad cells to paint the pattern; arrow keys move the tip vertically or horizontally. RULE: The tip only passes through the narrow segment when its width matches the opening. TRAP: Assuming the tip shrinks centered on the shaft; it anchors left, requiring a rightward adjustment to align with the gap.

ESTABLISHED: Five positions cycle through seven states via UP. Target is the partner glyph rotated once, index offset by three. FAILED: Repeated UPs on position zero without advancing rotation or position. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the initial glyph or a simple color swap. CONTROLS: UP advances the state cycle; RIGHT moves to the next position. DOWN is suspected to reverse the cycle but remains unverified.

GOAL: Clear the level by dropping blocks to form a rectangle over the bins, using arrows to position and space to drop. CONTROLS: Arrows move the falling block horizontally; space releases it to fall and settle. RULE: Blocks must align to create a continuous wall structure that covers the yellow bins without gaps. TRAP: Assuming adjacent blocks connect automatically; precise alignment is required to form the solid barrier.

ESTABLISHED: H and V dials encode cap and U displacement; execution occurs only on timer expiry, not on click. Initial position remains unchanged until the timeout completes. FAILED: Clicking to set H=11111, V=00000 without waiting for the timer to expire produced no movement or result update. GOAL IS NOT: Simply arranging the dials to a specific pattern; the solid block is the evaluated output, not the input configuration. CONTROLS: Clicking dials toggles their bits. Clicking elsewhere burns timer actions. Only the timer reaching zero triggers the machine's evaluation and potential solution c

ESTABLISHED: The arm drags colors only when passing through them; R and N are adjacent at column 18. FAILED: Extending the arm right without first aligning it to b's row (13-16) failed to grab b. GOAL IS NOT: A simple horizontal line; the solution likely requires vertical alignment or L-shaped chains. CONTROLS: UP/DOWN shifts the arm's row. LEFT/RIGHT moves the tip; passing through a color drags it.

GOAL: Capture three rotating sentries using a 19-move path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; sentries rotate and project danger zones. RULE: Death occurs only if the player ends a move two tiles ahead of a sentry’s facing. TRAP: Believing moving through a sentry’s current position is safe; you must capture it to clear its line.

GOAL: Arrange six colored tiles and two heads across three boxes to match a target color sequence. CONTROLS: Click items to select; click destinations to swap. Space submits the arrangement. RULE: Expanding a box reveals its contents, allowing nested placement of heads and tiles. TRAP: Assuming boxes are independent containers; they actually nest, requiring cross-box item movement.

GOAL: Align the player's yellow segment with a distant gap by adjusting column heights. CONTROLS: Click columns to shift their height values up or down. RULE: Bridges form only where adjacent column heights match within a window. TRAP: Assuming bridges persist after height changes; they vanish immediately when values diverge.

GOAL: Align each colored cross so its arms cover matching targets. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active cross; Space switched between them. RULE: Crosses act as infinite lines; targets are hit if on the same row or column as the center. TRAP: Believing arm length limits coverage. The lines extend fully, not just the visible pixel range.

GOAL: Extend the green and yellow bars until their tips reach the red crosses. CONTROLS: Clicking a slot below a bar lengthens that bar by three units. RULE: Both bars share the same starting distance to their targets, allowing parallel progress. TRAP: Assuming the increment was fixed at three for all pieces; it actually varies by piece type.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow tile aligns with the fixed bracket. CONTROLS: Red arrows rotate the ring clockwise; blue arrows rotate it counter-clockwise. RULE: The bracket marks the target position; alignment triggers the win condition. TRAP: Assuming the bracket moves with the ring wastes time; it remains stationary.

GOAL: Connect the white and gray points with a line passing through the ring. CONTROLS: Click empty cells to move the white point; click the gray point to draw the connecting line. RULE: The line must intersect the ring’s center to complete the circuit. TRAP: Assuming the ring is a barrier rather than a required waypoint.

GOAL: Cover all orange targets using plus-shaped arms of length 13. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selector; SPACE cycled through available shapes. RULE: A target is covered if it lies on the plus's row or column within arm distance. TRAP: Assuming any intersection of row/column distances covered targets; only exact alignment on the plus's arms works.

GOAL: Clear the grid by moving the marker using the crosses. CONTROLS: Click a cross to reveal valid moves. Click a green marker to execute that move. RULE: A cross only lights up if it shares a row or column with the marker. TRAP: Clicking a cross does not move the marker; you must click the resulting green dot.

GOAL: Reach the top exit with the matching symbol. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece through the corridor. RULE: Only matching symbols allowed passage into the exit panel. TRAP: Believing reaching the target cell alone ended the level; the exit required physical arrival at the top panel.

GOAL: Make the bottom-right quadrant match its center pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color. RULE: The center pattern is a legend: gray means blue, white means red. TRAP: Assuming the center pattern was decorative or unrelated to the quadrant's target state.

GOAL: Match the grid’s color pattern to the target shown by the special cells, using blue and orange. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between blue and orange. RULE: The two special cells in the middle column define the required pattern for the rest of the grid. TRAP: Assuming the top-right indicator was a score or timer, rather than a color legend.

GOAL: Arrange colored chains to fill the target area without overlapping walls. CONTROLS: Clicking a color extends or retracts its chain by three units. RULE: Chains must never intersect walls, even during intermediate moves. TRAP: Assuming final positions alone determine validity; extending green right before shrinking it left caused collisions with the vertical wall.

GOAL: Cover six scattered dots using intersecting diagonal lines, with the horizontal line providing coverage for the top targets. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected shape; SPACE cycled selection between the X, diamond, and horizontal line. RULE: A dot is covered if it lies on any active line segment, regardless of intersection points. TRAP: Believing the horizontal line covered all top dots led to missing a target at column 27, which required repositioning the horizontal line's center.

GOAL: Move the yellow marker to both bracket positions using a sequence of rotations. CONTROLS: Red buttons rotated the grid forward; green buttons rotated it backward. RULE: The solution required alternating directions to position the marker without overshooting the target. TRAP: Assuming green was merely a reset or undo, rather than a distinct backward rotation, led to incorrect move sequences.

GOAL: Raise both markers to the top of the orange columns. CONTROLS: Arrows move markers; UP advances a rising wall phase. RULE: Markers rise only when the wall’s gate aligns with their column. TRAP: Left marker at the top does not block right marker movement; UP still advances the phase.

GOAL: Paint the grid using color rules from special center cells. CONTROLS: Click to cycle colors or rotate patterns. RULE: White bits in a pattern mean "center color"; gray bits mean "other color." TRAP: Assuming gray always meant red; it actually meant orange for orange-centered cells.

ESTABLISHED: Lock is rows 32-36, cols 11-15. White token starts inside. Down action shifts tokens downward; white moves to row 34, cyan to 37. Timer bar decreases. FAILED: Pressing Down did not clear the lock or unlock the door. The wave animation completes without success. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the white token down the column. CONTROLS: Down arrow moves tokens vertically. No other controls tested.

GOAL: Transform the grid so every special cell’s eight neighbors match the predicted pattern, using the fewest clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking a special cell applies its rule to its eight neighbors, changing their colors. RULE: Green neighbors become red; white neighbors become blue; the special cell’s own color determines the transformation. TRAP: Assuming a neighbor’s color is determined solely by one adjacent special; overlapping influence requires checking all neighboring specials.

ESTABLISHED: Four RIGHT moves park gray at (8,38), retracting the red blob and opening (38,14). The gray stays put once its recorded path ends. FAILED: Recording extra moves before the blue reached (8,38) caused gray to shift off that spot, re-blocking the path. GOAL IS NOT: A simple straight-line route; timing gray’s parking is essential to clear the red obstacle. CONTROLS: RIGHT moves gray along the top track. SPACE locks in the recorded sequence. DOWN and RIGHT move the blue toward the target.

GOAL: Guide the yellow token to the exit by rotating the surrounding tiles. CONTROLS: Red arrows shifted tiles backward along the path; green arrows shifted them forward. RULE: Each click rotated the entire ring of tiles one step, changing which tile sat under the yellow token. TRAP: Assuming green and red arrows were simple inverses led to wasted clicks; their effects depended on the current tile arrangement, not just direction.

GOAL: Guide the blue dot to the bottom-right corner while managing a moving gray obstacle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the dot; Space records a path for the gray dot to replay. RULE: The gray dot stops moving when its recorded path ends, allowing safe passage. TRAP: Assuming blocked moves count as path steps wastes time; they are ignored in the recording.

GOAL: Connect colored endpoints to form unbroken lines across the grid. CONTROLS: Click an endpoint to select it, then click a destination to move or swap positions. RULE: Lines must pass only through empty cells; endpoints act as anchors, not obstacles. TRAP: Assuming lines can cross existing chains. They cannot; overlapping paths invalidate the connection.

GOAL: Extend colored bands to cover specific intersections without overlapping walls or each other. CONTROLS: Clicking a color lengthens its band by three units; clicking again shortens it. RULE: Bands cannot pass through solid obstacles, including the purple wall blocking the sky's path. TRAP: Assuming the purple block was a target rather than a barrier caused wasted extension attempts.

ESTABLISHED: Two podiums on the right (top red, bottom blue). Left has a chain of blocks (yellow, P1, red/darkred, gray, P4, green). FAILED: Setting P2 red or P4 blue with various green positions did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply making the left side a single connected piece. CONTROLS: Toggle switches change block colors (red/blue). Green block moves to different positions. No other actions succeeded.

GOAL: Slide the white T-piece right to fill the green piece's right-side gap, closing the red bridge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the white piece; only the white piece responds. RULE: The white piece's cavity accepts the green piece's right bar when aligned correctly. TRAP: Assuming the left column fits the cavity; the right bar is the correct insertion target.

GOAL: Slide the black piece so its gray mirror covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the black piece; the mirror moved opposite. RULE: Reflection across the center divider meant left became right. TRAP: Believing the black piece itself needed to touch the yellow target.

GOAL: Guide the tip to the head by clearing the magenta barrier. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; absorption consumes adjacent barriers. RULE: The gray wave erases obstacles along its path, opening the corridor. TRAP: Assuming the magenta ring blocks the way permanently; it is fuel, not a wall.

GOAL: Fill the top half of the block white and the bottom half purple to match the panel. CONTROLS: Click colors to select; SPACE fills the half facing the bracket; arrows rotate the bracket around the block. RULE: The bracket acts as a directional brush, painting only the side it opens toward. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the bracket linearly rather than rotating it around the perimeter.

GOAL: Guide the chain's free tip to the cross. CONTROLS: Click to extend the yellow segments outward. RULE: Only the uncapped end counts as the tip; the dot follows it. TRAP: Thinking any covered cell wins. The cross must be the specific free end, not a middle segment.

GOAL: Move green and yellow tokens to specific bands using four sliding bridges. CONTROLS: Click a bridge to slide it horizontally; tokens crossing a bridge shift with it. RULE: A bridge connects adjacent bands only when its column ranges overlap perfectly. TRAP: Assuming bridges move only one token; they actually transport all tokens currently intersecting their span.

GOAL: Recolor the orange chip by moving the cursor to its slot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor along the track; Space applies color. RULE: Movement follows a specific path, not a full circle; missing edges cause no-ops. TRAP: Assuming the track is a closed loop wastes time on invalid connections.

GOAL: Position the reflected piece to cover the yellow target. CONTROLS: SPACE switches selection between the divider and the black piece. Arrows move the selected object. The white dots mark the active piece. RULE: The blue piece is always the mirror image of the black piece across the divider. TRAP: Assuming vertical arrows are always disabled. They move the black piece when selected, allowing the reflection to reach lower targets.

ESTABLISHED: The player moves horizontally at row 37. Rightward movement into aligned corridor columns triggers vertical maze scrolling. Room C has a downward exit at columns 43-47, but no visible upward corridor due to a green wall. FAILED: Attempting to advance through blocked upper columns in Room C. Assuming vertical player movement is possible. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the right edge of the current room. CONTROLS: Left/Right moves the player. Alignment with open corridors causes scrolling. No vertical controls observed.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding moving threats and a stationary shooter. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile per press. RULE: Capturing the shooter removes its line of fire, opening the path. TRAP: Thinking you must dodge the shooter rather than capture it wasted time.

GOAL: Guide the blue dot to the pocket while managing echo timing and blob positions. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue dot; SPACE resets the level. RULE: Echoes park early to clear paths; blobs retract when specific nodes are occupied. TRAP: Assuming the blue enters the junction at move 14, when it actually occurs at move 13.

GOAL: Align the upper-left and lower-left white strips to equal length to form a bridge. CONTROLS: Click the top-right button to extend the upper-right strip and shrink the lower-left. Click the bridge to complete the level. RULE: The bridge appears only when the left strips match exactly. TRAP: White dashes above and below the bridge are decorations, not part of the strips. Don't count them when checking alignment.

GOAL: Guide yellow to (45,45) and orange to (45,51) on intersecting loops. CONTROLS: Left/right arrows rotate the horizontal loop; up/down arrows rotate the vertical loop. RULE: All arrows of the same direction act globally on the same loop, regardless of which cross they belong to. TRAP: Assuming each cross has independent local loops wastes time; movement is coupled across the entire board.

GOAL: Cover all four yellow targets using moving blocks and their mirror images. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; SPACE cycles selection between blocks and the divider. RULE: The divider reflects block positions across its line; moving blocks down places their mirrors up. TRAP: Assuming blocks stay put. You must move both black blocks down to align their reflections with the upper yellows.

GOAL: Route two shapes to cover all targets without overlapping. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape. Space switches which shape is active. RULE: Shapes cover targets along their full path, not just the final position. TRAP: Assuming Space selects the next shape in order; it actually cycles the current selection, requiring verification before moving.

GOAL: Cover the yellow cross with two black pieces and slide the divider to position 28. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected pieces three units; Space cycles selection. RULE: Pieces can overlap; only the final covering positions matter. TRAP: Assuming collision blocks movement wastes time; overlapping is allowed.

GOAL: Navigate past moving hazards to reach the exit using only six moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one tile in the indicated direction. RULE: Hazard positions are predictable; timing the crossing avoids collisions. TRAP: Assuming hazards move uniformly; their speeds and patterns vary, requiring precise observation of specific trajectories.

GOAL: Align both colored dots onto their matching cross targets simultaneously. CONTROLS: Clicking extends or retracts each colored bar by three units. RULE: A bar’s dot sits at its tip; bars must not overlap obstacles or each other. TRAP: Winning requires both dots on crosses, not just one; fixing the first alone did not clear the level.

ESTABLISHED: Green block (37,43) hides extra dots; (52,55) is a white endpoint inside the N ring. FAILED: Filtering dots by body exclusion alone, as the ring overlaps the endpoint. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching raw dot lists without handling ring/endpoint overlaps. CONTROLS: Dot detection ignores same-color neighbors but excludes ring pixels, hiding the endpoint.

GOAL: Move the diamond to the right, then down to touch the red palette and fill the red targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece. Space switches which piece is active. RULE: Touching a palette recolors the piece; the new color persists even after moving away. TRAP: Thinking the piece must stay on the palette to keep the color. It does not.

GOAL: Collect four colored chips to unlock the bracket’s final position. CONTROLS: Click chips to select; arrows rotate the bracket around the block; click the bracket to place it. RULE: Rotation direction depends on the bracket’s current angle, not a fixed clockwise or counterclockwise setting. TRAP: Assuming P225 to P270 moves UP; it actually moves DOWN, wasting time on invalid rotations.

GOAL: Guide the shrinking tip through the corridor to destroy the M square and reach the head. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the tip; clicks absorbed lines to clear obstacles. RULE: Waves traveled left along the tip's row, destroying blockers in their path. TRAP: Assuming the corridor to the head was open at the tip's current height; it was only passable further down.

GOAL: Move two yellow tiles to the bracketed cells on the top edge. CONTROLS: Four rotation buttons shift tiles along specific paths; green buttons undo the red ones. RULE: Each button applies a fixed permutation to tile positions, independent of color. TRAP: Assuming rotations affect all tiles uniformly; they only move tiles on specific tracks.

GOAL: Paint the canvas with four colored regions using half-plane fills and one stripe. CONTROLS: Click colors to select; SPACE applies the main bracket’s fill; click small brackets for stripes; arrows rotate the bracket. RULE: Fills overwrite existing colors, so order determines the final pattern. TRAP: Assuming all visible colors must be explicitly painted; leaving some white was correct.

GOAL: Paint the 9x9 grid with four colors, including a red stripe on the top edge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotated the bracket's position. Clicks selected colors and triggered fills. RULE: Fills covered half-planes defined by the bracket's angle, allowing overlapping layers to shape regions. TRAP: Believing the red stripe required a separate fill layer; it was actually the top of the blue layer.

GOAL: Position the piece and align both dividers to enclose exactly 90 extra gray cells. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; SPACE cycles selection between the piece and the divider assembly. RULE: With dividers selected, UP/DOWN moves the horizontal bar, LEFT/RIGHT moves the vertical bar. TRAP: Assuming selection persists after moving one divider; it often stays on the moved bar, causing the next directional input to be ignored.

GOAL: Eliminate all red targets without crossing orange patrol lines. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn. RULE: Orange enemies follow fixed paths; capturing a target instantly clears its associated danger zone. TRAP: Capturing a target does not expand the enemy's patrol range.

GOAL: Align three rotating tiles to central cells using paired swaps. CONTROLS: Click pairs to exchange tile positions along defined paths. RULE: Swaps act as simultaneous rotations; order determines final alignment. TRAP: Assuming single-tile moves or independent cycles; swaps affect all three tiles at once, requiring precise sequence planning rather than individual positioning.

ESTABLISHED: The block is not selectable by clicking. Walls rise from the bottom wall and spread sideways at the prong level (rows 12-13), filling the bins. The 12-wide landing test confirmed walls pass row 12 without spreading when prongs are absent. FAILED: Clicking the block or pedestal with LEFT arrow did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the block left. CONTROLS: LEFT arrow moves walls/blocks. Mouse clicks on block/pedestal are no-ops.

ESTABLISHED: Clicks pull the nearest piece toward the cursor. Pieces merge only when close enough; distant collisions are rejected. FAILED: Clicking empty space between pieces to force a merge. Repeatedly clicking the same target without adjusting position. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving pieces to adjacent grid cells without satisfying the proximity threshold for merging. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks select and move pieces. No keyboard or drag inputs were tested or observed.

GOAL: Route four colored endpoints to their matching blocks on a circular track. CONTROLS: Click an endpoint to select it, then click a destination to move or swap positions. RULE: Endpoints must connect to blocks of the same color without crossing paths. TRAP: Extra white pixels near the endpoint are a visual highlight, not additional obstacles or targets.

GOAL: Move the hub carrying a cross to the bottom board's exit, then jump over a board cross to merge them into one. CONTROLS: Click the hub to select it. Use directional keys to slide the hub along the outer track. Click a cross to initiate a jump. RULE: The hub acts as a temporary storage cell outside the main grid, allowing crosses to be routed around the border. TRAP: Assuming the hub moves independently of its contents; the cross travels with the hub until explicitly jumped.

GOAL: Slide two tokens to marked spots in linked rooms. CONTROLS: Arrows push tokens; clicks select or confirm. RULE: Tokens slide until hitting walls or other tokens, not just one step. TRAP: Assuming tokens stop at room edges; they continue sliding through open junctions into adjacent rooms.

GOAL: Guide the character through a winding path to the exit without running out of energy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character one step in the selected direction. RULE: Passing specific markers restores energy, allowing longer routes than the initial supply. TRAP: Assuming markers are decorative; ignoring them causes early exhaustion before reaching the exit.

ESTABLISHED: White prongs merge on contact; SPACE resets green pin. Moving white drags yellow pins, stretching arms. FAILED: Merging white prongs alone. Direct translation to blue pins failed due to arm length mismatch (right arm 7 units short). GOAL IS NOT: Simple overlap of white prongs and blue pins without arm extension or rotation. CONTROLS: Arrow keys translate white, dragging connected yellow pins. SPACE resets green pin or rotates assembly.

ESTABLISHED: Orange collects boxes and deposits into bar cells; it filled one cell in roughly sixteen actions. Five cells need filling. Budget is tight. FAILED: Player oscillation did not fill cells. Orange alone appears too slow for the remaining budget. GOAL IS NOT: A single-box delivery or player-only carrying. CONTROLS: RIGHT and LEFT move the player horizontally; blocked moves still consume time. Orange acts autonomously.

ESTABLISHED: The blue dot moves along recorded paths. Echoes persist and interact. Recording captures the current movement sequence. FAILED: Attempting to salvage the current state by overwriting old echoes without a timer reset. Waiting for the timer to expire did not yield a usable starting condition. GOAL IS NOT: A simple pathfinding challenge where the destination is reached by a single continuous move. CONTROLS: SPACE records the current movement as a new echo. Arrow keys move the blue dot. The timer counts down per attempt.

GOAL: Collect the object and exit using a limited energy bar that drains with every move. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; the bar decreases by one per action. RULE: Yellow squares refill the energy bar completely when touched, enabling long routes. TRAP: Assuming the bar refills automatically or that oscillating is harmless; it wastes critical actions.

ESTABLISHED: Markers always share the same row, moving together. The central pipe stays fixed; the M/p shape never moves. FAILED: Aligning markers to red gaps and pressing DOWN only causes a bounce. No action shifts the M/p or pipe. GOAL IS NOT: Merging markers across the pipe, or simply landing them on the red bar. CONTROLS: UP and DOWN move both markers vertically together. Horizontal movement does not separate them.

GOAL: Combine two small pieces into a larger one to clear the level. CONTROLS: Clicking a piece moves it toward the next click, merging if close enough. RULE: Pieces merge when their centers are within roughly five units of each other. TRAP: Assuming movement distance limits were strict; conservative estimates worked, but tighter constraints weren't always necessary.

GOAL: Clear the first level by moving the player. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; mouse clicks interact with cells. RULE: Openings require empty space above and below a barrier. TRAP: Clicking solid black walls without clearing obstacles above them wastes time.

GOAL: Move tokens through rooms to reach the exit lock. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected token; clicks change selection. RULE: Adjacent same-color tokens merge into one larger piece. TRAP: Assuming pieces stay separate wastes moves; merged pieces are harder to control and may exceed size filters.

ESTABLISHED: Three boards (A, B, C) connect via corridors. Two hubs sit at B's left exits. Hub 1 carries a cross. Delivery reduces the total count. FAILED: Attempting to jump over non-existent cells at column 84. Assuming adjacent rows 18 and 30 share a cell. GOAL IS NOT: Emptying board B's leftmost column or moving a cross to the far right edge. CONTROLS: Clicking a hub selects it. Clicking a landing spot executes a jump or delivery.

ESTABLISHED: L5 grid is 5x5 with symbols g, W, b, R, O. L4 solutions confirmed position-dependent color mapping for symbols around centers. FAILED: Uniform targets pcount9 and pcount18. Symmetric matrix assumptions. Timeout occurred. GOAL IS NOT: A uniform count pattern or simple symmetry. CONTROLS: Clicking selects operators. Submitting tests target configurations. No undo or reset observed.

GOAL: Cycle the object's color to blue by touching it repeatedly, then carry the symbol to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; touching the object advances its color and consumes the symbol. RULE: Colors follow a strict cycle: green, red, orange, blue. Leaving and returning makes the object reappear. TRAP: The object vanishes after being touched. Waiting for it to respawn is unnecessary; moving away and back restores it immediately.

GOAL: Rotate each column to match a target number sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selection bracket left/right. Up/Down cycles the selected column’s value. RULE: Values wrap around (e.g., 4 becomes 0). TRAP: Assuming the cursor position index matches the visual column index directly; off-by-one errors in coordinate calculation caused wasted moves.

GOAL: Align both markers on the same row with columns summing to 52 to pass the barrier. CONTROLS: Arrows move both markers simultaneously; the notch holds the left marker stationary. RULE: Holding one marker allows the other to change position without losing the vertical offset. TRAP: Assuming markers could be synchronized in the red bar; the offset is permanent there.

GOAL: Guide the cap into the U-shaped slot using beam timing. CONTROLS: Click H/V bits to toggle their state. Click the ball to launch the beam. RULE: The cap moves left only when the beam hits a black H bit; it stays on white. TRAP: Thinking the U moves independently. It is static; only the cap adjusts to the H pattern.

GOAL: Guide the player to the pink marker's column to clear the purple barrier. CONTROLS: Click to move the player left or right; click green blocks to remove them and open paths. RULE: Only columns aligned with the pink marker pass safely through the purple barrier's gaps. TRAP: The right-side corridor appears open but is blocked by the shifted purple barrier, leading to failure.

GOAL: Guide the green token to the yellow marker by switching piece colors to open paths. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green token; clicks toggle piece colors between blue (solid) and red (passable).
